I've been working this land for 35 years. I know Quzhou soil and I know what the seasons demand here. Let me think through this year.

My 12 mu splits naturally — 6 mu for cotton, which is my main income, and 6 mu for the wheat-maize rotation. Two people in the house means I have to be realistic about labor. I can't spread myself too thin. My husband helps but we're not young anymore.

**Cotton (6 mu):** I always plough deep before spring planting — maybe late April. I've used Bt hybrid cotton for years now. It cuts down the bollworm spraying. But aphids and spider mites still come in summer, so I'll need to walk the field and spray. I water at seedling if it's dry, again at first square, and again at peak bolling. Well water is reliable so I'm not worried. Base fertilizer goes in at planting, then I topdress urea when the bolls are setting.

**Wheat (6 mu):** I plant in mid-October after the soil cools. I buy whatever improved variety the county seed station sells — Jimai or similar. I always do a pre-sowing irrigation if the soil is dry, then the yuèdōng water before it freezes, and again at jointing. Heading spray for aphids and powdery mildew. I plough before sowing.

**Summer Maize (6 mu, same land as wheat):** Right after wheat harvest in early June, I don't have time for deep tillage. I rotary till and get seeds in fast. Hybrid seed — I've never gone back to traditional. I water at tasseling if we get a dry stretch in July. Herbicide early, then watch for corn borer. Harvest by late September before I'm too busy with cotton picking.
